subject: Spectrogram scale is changed after filtering with fir()

messages.author: c475911f3ec29d78
messages.subject: Spectrogram scale is changed after filtering with fir()
parts:
Hello, I am trying to use a hi-pass filter to remove frequencies below 1000 Hz. However, when I apply the filter, the resulting spectrogram has the wrong scale on the y-axis. By comparing the two spectrograms visually, it looks like the correct frequencies are filtered out, but I can't for the life of me figure out why the scale is wrong after filtering. Any help is greatly appreciated! My code is below, and spectrogram images are attached.

  ## hi-pass
a<- (note)
spectro(a, wl = 512, wn = "hanning", zp = 0, ovlp = 80)
b<- fir(a, from=1000)
spectro(b, f=6262, wl = 512, wn = "hanning", zp = 0, ovlp = 80)


Thank you!
Molly

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Spectrogram scale is changed after filtering with fir()
parts:
Dear Molly,

I do not know what was the sampling frequency of your object a but you specify f=6262 when plotting the spectrogram of b.
a and b should have the sample sampling frequency.
You might use output="Wave" to be sure to save the sampling frequeny.

This test seems to work:

data(tico)
spectro(tico)
filter <- fir(tico, from=4000, output="Wave")
spectro(filter)

HTH

Jerome
